title: Kafka Producer
description: The producer app's Kafka client: throughput, errors, latency, batching, back-pressure, JVM.

options.content: **Kafka Producer** — the producer app's own Kafka client metrics. Filter by **source** (docker container / app on your machine) and **client_id** above. Best-practice signals, in order: *throughput* (sends/s), *errors and retries*, *latency* (queue time + request latency), *batching efficiency*, and *back-pressure* (buffer, in-flight requests). Most panels show a value only while messages are being sent.

panels.title: Records sent / s
panels.description: Records the producer sent per second (1-minute average).

panels.title: Errors / s
panels.description: Records that failed after all retries. Should be 0.

panels.title: Retries / s
panels.description: Retried records, e.g. while a partition leader moves. Short bursts are fine; constant retries are not.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Average time from sending a produce request to the broker's answer.

panels.title: Buffer used
panels.description: Share of buffer.memory (32 MB) holding records not yet sent. Near 100% = send() blocks.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Produce requests sent and waiting for an answer. Max 5 per broker connection by default.

panels.title: Records sent / s
panels.description: Records sent per second by each producer client.

panels.title: Records sent / s by topic
panels.description: Per-topic send rate. The per-topic metrics appear after the first send to a topic.

panels.title: Bytes sent / s
panels.description: Network bytes sent to the brokers, including protocol overhead.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Produce request round trip to the broker. With acks=all it includes replication to the in-sync replicas.

panels.title: Record queue time
panels.description: How long records wait in the producer buffer before being sent: linger.ms plus waiting for a free in-flight slot. Growing queue time = the producer can't send as fast as you call send().

panels.title: send() until ack (KafkaTemplate)
panels.description: What the application sees: queue time + request latency, measured by Spring around each send.

panels.title: Batch size
panels.description: Bytes per batch, per partition. The dashed line is batch.size (16 KB): batches reaching it are full. Small batches under load = raise linger.ms.

panels.title: Records per request
panels.description: Records carried by each produce request. Higher = fewer, more efficient requests.

panels.title: Record size
panels.description: Size of a record (key + value + headers). Watch the max against max.request.size (1 MB).

panels.title: Compression rate
panels.description: Compressed size / original size of the batches. 1 = no compression (compression.type=none, the default).

panels.title: Errors and retries / s
panels.description: Errors = lost records (after delivery.timeout.ms, 2 min). Retries are usually leader changes.

panels.title: Failed sends by error type
panels.description: Why sends failed, as seen by the application, e.g. TimeoutException when brokers are unreachable.

panels.title: Batch splits and buffer exhausted / s
panels.description: Batch split: a batch was too large for the broker. Buffer exhausted: send() gave up after max.block.ms because the buffer stayed full. Both should be 0.

panels.title: Buffer memory
panels.description: Records waiting to be sent. When used reaches total, send() blocks for up to max.block.ms (60 s).

targets.expr: max by (client_id) (kafka_producer_buffer_total_bytes{application="producer", source=~"$source", client_id=~"$client_id"} - kafka_producer_buffer_available_bytes{application="producer", source=~"$source", client_id=~"$client_id"})

panels.title: Waiting for buffer
panels.description: Share of time threads were blocked in send() waiting for buffer space, and how many threads wait now. Anything above 0 = the brokers can't keep up with the producer.

panels.title: Requests in flight and throttling
panels.description: Requests awaiting an answer, and time the broker throttled the producer because of a quota (0 here).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Open connections (one per broker it talks to, plus bootstrap). Constant creating/closing = connection problems or connections.max.idle.ms too low.

panels.title: Network thread busy
panels.description: How the producer's network thread spends its time. I/O ratio near 1 = the single sender thread is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Metadata age
panels.description: Seconds since the producer last refreshed cluster metadata (leaders). Refreshed every metadata.max.age.ms (5 min) or after an error.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: API calls by URI and HTTP status: 201 sent, 400 invalid, 500 Kafka error.

panels.title: Response time
panels.description: /api/messages answers after the broker ack, so this includes the Kafka send time.

targets.expr: sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{application="producer", source=~"$source", uri=~"/api/.*"}[1m])) / sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{application="producer", source=~"$source", uri=~"/api/.*"}[1m]))

panels.title: Response time p95, with traces
panels.description: 95th percentile response time of the /api endpoints. The dots are exemplars: single requests with their trace id. Hover a dot and click "Query with Tempo" to open that request's trace: HTTP, Kafka send and the consumer's processing.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application="producer", source=~"$source", uri=~"/api/.*"}[1m])))

panels.title: Heap used vs max
panels.description: Heap in use and the limit. Used close to max for a long time = memory pressure, long GCs.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Time the JVM was stopped for garbage collection. Long pauses delay sends, polls and heartbeats.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the app, and by the whole machine (container), as a share of all cores.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Live and blocked threads. Each Kafka client adds a few network / heartbeat threads.
